title: Prayer Silence Icons
lede: Round 2 of the launcher icon for «أوقات الصلاة تونس». Every proposal now shows the app's main job: the phone goes quiet while you pray. A prayer rug replaces the mosque architecture of round 1, and the colours come from Kairouan carpets, Sidi Bou Said blue and Nabeul clay instead of dark teal and gold.
Best first. Switch the launcher mask below to see each icon the way different phones cut it.

proposals.idea: A Kairouan prayer rug with a mute badge, the way a video call marks a muted person.
proposals.silence: The speaker with a × is the phone's own mute sign. It reads at once, down to 36 px.
proposals.prayer: A fringed rug seen from above, in Sidi Bou Said blue with one Kairouan lozenge. No building and no crescent.
proposals.risk: Read literally, it says the rug is muted. The × stays inside the badge and never touches the rug, but you should be comfortable with that reading.

variants.label: Do Not Disturb moon instead of the ×

proposals.idea: The prayer rug is the phone's volume slider, pushed all the way down to mute.
proposals.silence: The white knob holds the mute sign at the foot of the track, like Android's volume panel at zero.
proposals.prayer: A madder-red Kairouan rug with white wool fringe and one lozenge.
proposals.risk: The slider idea only lands for people who know the volume panel. Everyone else still sees a rug and a mute sign. In the themed icon the fringe can look like the pins of a chip.

variants.label: Striped kilim ends instead of a border

proposals.idea: The crescent is the sign of Islam and also the Do Not Disturb icon on Samsung, Xiaomi, Oppo and iPhone. Here it shelters a prayer rug.
proposals.silence: It looks like the Do Not Disturb tile switched on. Clear for Samsung and Xiaomi users, weaker on Pixel, where Do Not Disturb is a circle with a bar.
proposals.prayer: The crescent, and a cream rug with a madder prayer niche.
proposals.risk: Many people will read the crescent as the hilal first, so silence is the second reading. A crescent holding an object is a common pattern among prayer apps.

variants.label: Daylight: blue crescent on pale sky

proposals.idea: One calligraphic ش, the letter Arabic uses to write "shh". Its teeth step down and its tail fades out like a ring dying away.
proposals.silence: Arabic readers hear «ششش», and the fading tail helps. Nothing shows a phone.
proposals.prayer: Only through the app's name. No religious sign is used.
proposals.risk: It can pass for the logo of a café, a pottery brand or a keyboard app. It is the most stylish of the four and the least literal, so it may suit a splash screen or wordmark better than the launcher.

dropped.why: At icon size the lips looked like a cosmetics ad.
Read as a paperclip or the letter e, not as the ⊖ sign.
The raised hands looked like rubber gloves.
Read as a dumbbell with a chip in the middle, and a waveform says audio, not silence.

next: Tell me which one you want, and which variant if any. I will turn it into the real Android icon: vector layers, a themed-icon layer for Android 13 and later, fresh PNG fallbacks and the 512 px Play Store image.
If none is right but one comes close, tell me what to change and I will push that direction further.
footer: How these were made: 30 ideas from 5 angles, scored by 3 judges; 8 drawn and checked at real launcher sizes; 4 kept after two critique rounds. These are mockups only: the app still ships its old icon. Source SVGs, notes and previews are in android-app/logo-proposals/round2.
